correctness.rationale: The explicitly normalized Hermite ambiguity functions reduce the claim to squares of two Laguerre polynomials. At t0=3-sqrt(5) both squares equal 9-4sqrt(5), giving a universal upper certificate. The exact factorization with a square times a strictly positive quadratic proves a global lower certificate at w*=1-1/sqrt(5), and the derivative at the positive interior contact t0 establishes the unique optimizing weight. Algebraic identities were checked symbolically and the underlying Hermite normalization independently checked by numerical integral. This proves only the stated Gaussian-normalized pointwise gain.

value.rationale: Alaifari--Yang identify complementary Hermite ambiguity zeros as the practical obstacle in direct STFT phase retrieval. The first non-Gaussian two-window pair is the smallest pair with independent nontrivial radial zeros. The theorem solves its natural fixed-total-precision uniform Gaussian-envelope coverage problem completely: exact positive margin, unique exposure split, and sharp worst-case circle. It supplies a guaranteed two-channel local inversion sensitivity on every bounded aperture, rather than only qualitative absence of common zeros. The choice of envelope is the common intrinsic Hermite Gaussian factor, not an arbitrary radial cutoff. It does not claim global unweighted or nonlinear recovery stability.
